## Behavior (per `specs/csv.md` + RFC 4180)
- Single pass, no backtracking: LF/CRLF/CR terminators (CRLF counted once), `,` separators, no trimming, Unicode preserved verbatim.
- Quoted fields: `""` → `"`, commas/newlines inside quotes preserved byte for byte (`\r\n` is not normalized); field content copied via zero-copy slices, `StringBuilder` only when an escape occurs.

## What was built

A genuine line-scanner + value-parser + printer for this repo's INI dialect, organized by concern in the root `ini` package (so `@ini.parse` / `@ini.print` stay where the tests expect them):

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [ini.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/ini.mbt) | `parse`: the line loop, section bookkeeping, entry assembly |
| [scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/scanner.mbt) | line splitting (LF/CRLF), separator lookup, inline-comment stripping, key validation, section headers |
| [value_parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/value_parser.mbt) | the three value carriers: quote scanning, per-carrier escape decoding, continuation joining |
| [char_class.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/char_class.mbt) | character classification on UTF-16 code units |
| [printer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/printer.mbt) | `print`: always-double-quoted values, section names rendered so they read back unchanged |
| [error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/error.mbt) | `ParseError(line, reason)` |
| [README.md](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/README.md) | overview, architecture, algorithms, usage, testing, design rationale |

```diago
direction: down
input: StringView
lines: "split_lines → physical lines"
loop: "line loop"
fields: "key + value head"
value: "quoted | unquoted+continuations"
decode: "decode_escapes per carrier"
doc: "Doc { global, sections }"
input -> lines -> loop -> fields -> value -> decode -> doc
```

Key algorithm choices, all traceable to [specs/ini.md](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/specs/ini.md): continuation is decided on the **raw** line from the trailing-backslash *parity* before escapes collapse (`\\`→`a\`, `\\\`→`a\b=1`); continuation lines are appended verbatim and contribute text, not syntax (no comment stripping, no section detection); inline comments need a preceding whitespace code unit; the closing quote must be on the opening quote's physical line; duplicate keys/section re-opening fall out of storing entries in `Map`.

## What was built

A real, general INI parser and printer for this repo's dialect, in five focused modules of the root `ini` package:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_3/error.mbt) | `ParseError` suberror (1-based line + reason), `ParseError::message` |

| [scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_3/scanner.mbt) | physical lines → `LineKind` (blank/comment/section/entry); section headers, first-separator split, key validation, quoted values, inline comments, backslash continuations |
| [parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_3/parser.mbt) | document assembly: global vs. section placement, section re-open, last-wins duplicates |
| [printer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_3/printer.mbt) | `Doc` → INI text with an exactly reversible encoding (always double-quoted values, quote-wrapped section names when needed) |

Parsing is one pass: `split_lines` → `scan_line` → `LineKind` → `Doc`; the scanner never touches `Doc` and the parser knows nothing about quotes or escapes. Continuation is decided on raw text (odd/even trailing-backslash runs per `specs/ini.md`), then escapes are decoded once; a terminating line break does not fabricate an extra line, so a dangling marker is an error while a marker followed by a real blank line joins.

## Key decisions

- **Grammar whitelists, not a blacklist.** Each component is validated against its own ABNF production (`pchar`, `userinfo`, `reg-name`, `query`/`fragment`, `scheme`, `port`, `IP-literal`), so the whole excluded set (space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, `"`, controls, non-ASCII) falls out of one mechanism.
- **Scheme detection is the only non-delimiter split.** `a:b` is a URI with scheme `a`, `a/b:c` is a relative path; a `:` before any `/` therefore forces a valid scheme, otherwise the reference is rejected (`1http://h`, `ht_tp://h`, `://h`).
- **Presence ≠ emptiness** (`None` vs `Some("")`) end to end, so `x://@:?#` and `http://h/?` survive a round trip; ports stay text (`Some("")` legal, no range/leading-zero normalization).
- **Strict Section 5.2** (`http:g` stays `http:g`), with `remove_dot_segments` written as an index walk over the RFC's input buffer so the prefix-rewrite steps (`/./`, `/..`) behave exactly (`g/..` → `/`, `..g` stays).
- **Ambiguity is rejected**: multiple `@`, non-numeric ports, text after an IP literal, malformed brackets.

### Key implementation points

- **Streaming first:** nothing assumes one `read` fills a value. `read_exact` loops for 1/4/8-byte values; `read_payload` gathers a `LEN` payload into a buffer that *grows with bytes that actually arrive* (seeded at `min(n, 1024)`, doubling), so a `2^31-1` prefix on a short stream raises immediately instead of reserving 2 GB; `skip_payload` discards through a fixed 1 KB scratch buffer.
- **Varints:** one 64-bit reader implements the ten-byte limit, accepts non-minimal forms (`80 00` is 0), keeps only bit 63 of a tenth byte (`80×9 7F` → `2^63`), raises on an eleventh continuation byte and on truncation. All 32-bit readers are that reader masked to the low 32 bits, which is what makes both the ten-byte sign-extended `int32=-1` and `FF FF FF FF 0F` decode to `-1`. Writers always emit minimal form; negative `int32`/`enum` are sign-extended to ten bytes; ZigZag is written on unsigned bits so `-2^31`/`-2^63` cannot overflow on decode.
- **Length-delimited:** every prefix goes through one `read_length` that enforces `0 ..= 2^31-1` (so `2^32`, whose low bits look small, is malformed); `string` payloads are validated against table 3-7 (overlongs, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncated, stray continuations) while NUL, C1 controls, noncharacters and a leading U+FEFF are kept.
- **Packed/unknown:** `read_packed` decodes through a `LimitedReader` window (a payload ending mid-varint or short of 4/8 fixed bytes raises even when the stream continues; a zero-progress guard prevents loops); `read_unknown` skips 0/1/2/5, recurses over nested groups with end-tag field-number matching, and raises for EGROUP/6/7.
- **Floats** are bit-exact (`-0.0`, infinities, NaN payloads) because reading/writing only reinterprets bits.

- **Presence vs emptiness** is carried by `Option`: `http://h?` gives `query = Some("")`, `http://h` gives `None`; `to_string` emits delimiters exactly when components are present, so `parse(uri.to_string()) == uri` holds (checked by the provided quickcheck test plus 1000 extra iterations locally).

### Key implementation points

- **Streaming**: every value is gathered across as many `read` calls as it takes (`read_byte`, `read_exactly`, chunked `read_payload`/`skip_exactly`); EOF inside a value always raises. `LimitedReader` confines packed decoding to exactly one payload.
- **Varints**: at most ten bytes, non-minimal forms accepted, tenth-byte bits beyond the 64th dropped, an eleventh byte raises, low-32-bit truncation for the 32-bit readers.
- **Keys**: `(field_number << 3) | wire_type`; wire types 0–5 returned, 6/7 and field number 0 raise.
- **Length prefixes** are checked as a full 64-bit varint against `2^31-1`, so 2^32 is rejected even though its low 32 bits look small; payloads are read in bounded chunks so hostile lengths cannot force huge allocations.
- **UTF-8** is implemented in-package (overlongs, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncations, stray continuations rejected; BOM/NUL/C1 kept), so the codec needs no extra package dependency.
- **Packed fields** stop exactly at the payload end; a payload ending mid-element raises; a stalled element decoder raises instead of looping.
- **Groups** are skipped recursively with field-number matching for the end tag; wire type 4 outside a group and 6/7 raise.
- Writers emit canonical minimal encodings; float/double bit patterns (NaN payloads, infinities, `-0.0`, subnormals) round-trip exactly.

### Key design points
- **Splitting, not pattern matching**: each delimiter is peeled at its own layer; a scheme-less first segment containing `:` is rejected (`path-noscheme`), which is what makes `1http://h`/`ht~tp://h` invalid while `a/b:c` stays legal.
- **Validation by whitelist** per component, so the whole forbidden-character family (space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, controls, malformed `%`-triplets, negative ports) is one code path. Non-ASCII, raw `[` in a query, and a second `#` are rejected deliberately and documented as such.
- **IPv6** collapses the ABNF's nine alternatives into one group-count rule (exactly 8 groups without `::`, ≤ 7 with it, IPv4 tail only last, `dec-octet` without leading zeros).
- **Resolution is strict** (`http:g` → `http:g`), with `remove_dot_segments` transcribed literally so all abnormal §5.4.2 cases hold.
- `to_string` emits a delimiter exactly when its component is present, so `parse(to_string(u)) == u`.
